paragraphs: Rabbi Yaakov. (Without further designation; he is Rabbi Yaakov ben Korshai, a Tanna mentioned in the Mishnah.) Hyman presents the accepted identification that Rabbi Yaakov without further designation is the one sometimes called Rabbi Yaakov Korshai, or ben Korshai, or Kodshai (identified as Elisha–Acher’s daughter’s son, an identification Hyman challenges below). The proof of this is that in Avot 4:16–17: “Rabbi Yaakov says: This world is like a vestibule before the world to come; prepare yourself

in the vestibule so that you may enter the banquet hall. He used to say: Better one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the world to come.” This saying is cited in Kohelet Rabbah 4:6 and at the beginning of Vayikra Rabbah, chapter 3: “Rabbi Yaakov bar Korshai said: Better a handful of quiet in the world to come than two handfuls of toil and striving after wind in this world. He used to say: Better one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the world to come,

for the world to come comes only by virtue of this world.” This Rabbi Yaakov was the Tanna in the Sanhedrin of Usha, as stated explicitly in Horayot 13b: when Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Natan formed a conspiracy between them to remove Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel from his patriarchate, they decided to ask him to teach tractate Uktzin, knowing that he was not expert in it, and through this they would bring their plan from potential to actuality. When Rabbi Yaakov ben Karshai heard (Dikdukei Soferim reads ben

Kodshai), he said: “Perhaps, Heaven forbid, the matter will come to shame” (for Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel). He went and sat behind Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel’s upper chamber, expounded, recited and repeated it; Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel understood his intent, paid attention and learned it, and through this he was saved from the upheaval. Of who his teachers were we find only that he spoke in Rabbi Meir’s name, as in Yevamot 102a, Gittin 14b and Bava Metzia 78b; but we find him as a colleague of the colleagues of

Rabbi Meir: he disagrees with Rabbi Yose, as in Nedarim 12b; with Rabbi Natan, in Kiddushin 79a; with Rabbi Shimon, as in Shabbat 144b (and this is from Tosefta Taharot, chapter 10), Kiddushin 57a (from Tosefta Negaim, chapter 8), and Bava Kamma 65a. Now in Kiddushin 39b and the end of Chullin: “It was taught: the school of Rabbi Yaakov says” (Hyman proposes “It was taught: Rabbi Yaakov says,” as cited in Tosefta Chullin, end of chapter 10, and in Dikdukei Soferim):

“There is no mitzvah in the Torah whose reward is stated beside it on which the resurrection of the dead does not depend … Rav Yosef said: Had Acher (Elisha) expounded this verse like Rabbi Yaakov, his daughter’s son, he would not have sinned.” Hyman asks how Rav Yosef knew that Rabbi Yaakov was Acher’s daughter’s son — something we do not find anywhere. And even supposing that he had it as a tradition, is it not known that Rabbi

Yaakov was Rabbi’s teacher, as we will explain further? If so, how is it possible to say that when Elisha’s daughters came to take charity from Rabbi, Rabbi decreed and said, “Let there be none to extend kindness to him, and none to be gracious to his orphans,” as cited in Chagigah, beginning of chapter 2? Likewise in Chagigah 15b, when Acher’s daughter came to Rabbi for support, he said to her, “Is there still of his seed in the world?” How could he say such a thing if his holy teacher

was this man’s daughter’s son? In truth, in the Jerusalem Talmud, Chagigah, beginning of chapter 2, Rav Yosef’s saying is cited in other language, for they said there: “And he (Acher) did not know that Rabbi Yaakov had expounded it before him, ‘that it may go well with you,’” etc.; the plain sense is that Rabbi Yaakov had already expounded this. Likewise the words “his daughter’s son” are absent in Dikdukei Soferim on Chullin there. Hyman considers the truth clear: Rabbi Yaakov was never

Acher’s daughter’s son; he proposes that Kiddushin and Chullin there originally read that Rav Yosef said, “Had Acher expounded this verse like Rabbi Yaakov bar Karshai,” and from the word Karshai it became corrupted into ‘berateih’ (his daughter’s son); and with this everything comes to its place in peace. Let us return to our subject. He was the Tanna in the Sanhedrin of Usha, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel entrusted his precious son to him

to study mishnayot and baraitot with him (for this was Rabbi Yaakov’s appointment, for he was expert by heart in all the mishnayot and baraitot). This is what they said in the Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat 10:5 and Pesachim, beginning of chapter 10, that Rabbi Yaakov ben Korshai was Rabbi’s teacher (but the reasoning of the mishnayot and their analysis Rabbi received from his father, from Rabbi Shimon and from his other teachers; only the correct readings did he receive from Rabbi Yaakov, as explained at length in his entry). And this is what we find in

Yoma 61a: “Rabbi said: Rabbi Yaakov taught me a distinction concerning the logs”; in Gittin 14a, “Rabbi said in the name of Rabbi Yaakov”; in Ketubot 7a he disagrees with him, but Rabbi conceded like Rabbi Yaakov; likewise in Chullin 45b he disagrees with him, and Rabbi ruled like Rabbi Yaakov. We find that he disagrees with Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Yehudah, as in Sukkah 4b and 26b and Beitzah 35b. Of those who speak in his name (besides Rabbi) we find:

Elazar ben Yehudah of Kefar Avelim, as in Zevachim 28a. Yehudah ben Nekisa in his name, as in Chullin 118b. There, 98a: “Rabbi Nachum said that Rabbi Biryim said in the name of an elder, and Rabbi Yaakov is his name.” Well known to all is what they said in Bava Kamma 39b: “A deaf-mute’s ox, an imbecile’s or a minor’s, that gored — Rabbi Yaakov pays half damages,” and they ask, “What has Rabbi Yaakov to do with it?”

He is likewise mentioned in Shevuot 3b, holding that one is not flogged for a prohibition involving no action, and disagreeing with Rabbi Yehudah. In Menachot 36a he disagrees with the sages and holds that one wears tefillin until the foot traffic ends from the market. In Bekhorot 7a he holds that the honey of gazin and hornets is forbidden. In Bereshit Rabbah, beginning of chapter 17, he said: “Whoever has no wife
lives without good, without help, without joy, without blessing, without atonement.”

notes.text: This notice is scan-derived, with sentences continuing between L-groups; their source portions and complete sequence remain intact. The opening conventional claim that Yaakov is Acher’s daughter’s son is intentionally followed by Hyman’s rejection and proposed קרשי→ברתיה corruption; the English attributes this argument and does not admit or merge a genealogy. ח״ש is interpreted as חס ושלום. TEVayikra3:1 has Yaakov bar Korshoi, supporting bar rather than an invented RabbiKorshai. NamedDavidsonBK39b asks what Yaakov has to do with paying and then emends to Yaakov says: he pays; the English deliberately preserves Yaakov pays so the objection remains intelligible. The supplied Gittin14a and14b locators are retained; the saved14b paragraph contains RabbiYehudahHaNasi reportingYaakov reportingMeir. The saved14a opening scalar is merely a bounded nonmatch, not a whole-folio absence claim. GuggenheimerJTChag2:1’s bounded connected Acher/Yaakov/daughters passage was read, not the entire long scalar; it gives Yaakov’s prior exposition without establishing Hyman’s proposed scribal history. His correct-readings-only teacher distinction and chronological arguments remain his account.

The consulted Vayikra Rabbah has Yaakov bar Korshoi, not an independently attested Rabbi Korshai. Bava Kamma 39b first prints Yaakov pays and then objects and emends it to Yaakov says; both steps explain the supplied quotation. The whole consulted Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2:1 scalar has now been read, including Yaakov’s prior interpretation and the daughters’ request for support; the current note truthfully recording an earlier bounded read is retained verbatim. These witnesses do not establish Hyman’s proposed קרשי-to-ברתיה copying history or admit or reject a genealogy on independent authority. His categorical rejection, accepted-identification framing and correct-readings-only teacher distinction remain attributed with their original force, and all scan-unit continuations remain intact.
